label: Original-phase input 0 or u, or a d/f/q/h/2/b input right after another such token
explanation: Fires only while the original tokens are being read (essentially never at <DEL> or during the copy phase). The input token sets it: 0 and u are the strongest triggers (about 39% active rate each, together ~58% of activation mass), then d and f, then a weaker group (q, h, 2, b). It looks like it builds up over a run: activations get larger when several trigger tokens arrive in a row (e.g. l c 2 [d h b e 0] climbing to 0.94 of max), and the active rate rises with position (orig_idx >= 4 is about 3x lift). Weaker triggers mostly need a trigger token just before them. Not active on most other letters (p, e, g are below base rate). The rule is graded and depends on history, so a boolean predicate tops out around F1 0.66: some isolated 0/u inputs early in the sequence stay silent, and weak tokens that follow a run of triggers are missed.
